reasoning: A familiar idiom for someone stingy or begrudging. The adjective is contracted in conversational pronunciation, and ق is glottalized.
This is the masculine past form, meaning 'he married' or 'he got married.' The metathesized variant تجوّز is also common.
As an intensifier, this is vulgar slang strongly associated with Egyptian Arabic, although some Palestinian speakers borrow it. It is not an unmarked Ramallah equivalent of كتير.
I read بيبين as bibayyin, 'be apparent'; bibiin is another possible spoken form. عليك addresses a man and has the long vowel ee.
Everyday urban pronunciation replaces ث with ت and glottalizes ق. The adjective has long ii.
Both appreciation and estimation are established meanings. This noun is used conversationally, normally with glottalized ق.
The conversational pronunciation commonly inserts a short vowel between س and ر. It is the ordinary word for a bridge.
This is the usual Arabic country name for Colombia. The borrowed name has some variation in vowel quality and length; o-vowels are natural in Palestinian speech.
This can introduce one side of a contrast, especially with من ناحية تانية. It also means 'from one perspective' or 'in terms of.'

This is the ordinary local name of the Dead Sea. بحر commonly has an inserted short vowel, and ميّت has doubled ي.
The ة is pronounced t in this construct phrase. ق is glottalized, while ط and ض remain emphatic.
A standard conversational bedtime wish addressed to a man. خير has Palestinian ee rather than the MSA diphthong ay.
The everyday ordinal is taani, with ت rather than ث. It can also mean 'another' in suitable contexts.
A conversational idiom for acting covertly or behind the scenes. The English captures its figurative meaning.
Besides physical heaviness, this can describe a tiresome or unwelcome person. ث becomes ت and urban ق is a glottal stop.
Dinya is a common Palestinian pronunciation, rather than formal dunya. The word means the world or worldly life and can also refer to surrounding conditions.
This is the ordinary term for an average, including a student's grade average. Conversational pronunciation commonly drops the initial unstressed vowel.
The English selects the masculine past form, 'he ignored' or 'he paid no attention.' ط is emphatic and ن is doubled.
The everyday masculine past form glottalizes initial ق and drops the final written hamza. The Arabic is respelled to reflect that pronunciation.
محتاج is masculine singular, and عملية here means a surgical operation. The subject 'he' can remain implicit in this conversational frame.
A normal Palestinian expression meaning 'wherever' or 'wherever it may be.' وين has long ee.
This is the everyday word for a broom. The final ة is pronounced e after س.
This noun is used in Palestinian conversation for belonging or affiliation. 'Identity' is related but is more directly expressed by هوية.
A blessing wishing someone opportunities, prosperity, or success. وجه is pronounced wijh here, and the suffix addresses a man.
